RUN.about: Cut by the developer journey of building a Flask web app — you create and configure the application, wire up routes and blueprints, handle incoming requests at runtime, render templates and JSON, then run and test it — the order every Flask project follows.

AUTHORED.title: Creating the App
AUTHORED.sub: Instantiate Flask, load configuration, define signals and type aliases — everything before the first route.
AUTHORED.detail: `Flask(__name__)` builds a two-tier class hierarchy (App → Flask), populates a `Config` dict with 26 defaults, creates a URL map, a JSON provider, and a CLI group.

group.note: These are the logical parts of creating a Flask application, not a strict sequence.

issues.detail: If a relative path is passed as instance_path, the constructor raises a ValueError with a message that might confuse users who expect it to be resolved from root_path.

issues.title: Static route uses weakref to avoid cycle
issues.detail: The static-file view function captures `self` via `weakref.ref(self)` and dereferences it on every call. If the app is garbage-collected while still serving, the dereference returns None and crashes.

issues.title: Setup changes after first request are silently blocked
issues.detail: `_check_setup_finished` raises AssertionError if any setup method (add_url_rule, register_blueprint, etc.) is called after the first request, but only if _got_first_request is True.

children.title: Default Configuration
children.sub: The 26-key default_config dict defined on the Flask class.
children.detail: Every Flask app starts with these defaults via `make_config`. With no `SECRET_KEY`, `get_signing_serializer` returns `None`, so a `NullSession` is used that raises `RuntimeError` on write.

code.label: make_config copies default_config into app config

issues.title: SECRET_KEY defaults to None
issues.detail: With no SECRET_KEY, get_signing_serializer returns None and open_session yields None, so Flask uses a NullSession that raises RuntimeError on any write attempt.

children.title: Configuration Loading
children.sub: The Config dict subclass and its six methods for loading settings from files, objects, env vars, and mappings.
children.detail: `Config` extends `dict` with methods to populate itself from Python files, modules, JSON/TOML, env vars, and plain mappings. Only UPPERCASE keys are accepted, and `ConfigAttribute` is a descriptor that proxies attribute access to the dict.

group.note: Independent loading methods, used in any combination.

anatomy.caption: Config loading sources and the uppercase-only filter
Config loading methods
rows: File path from env var → from_pyfile

issues.title: from_pyfile executes arbitrary code
issues.detail: `from_pyfile` calls `exec(compile(config_file.read(), ...))` on the file contents. Any Python code in the config file is executed with no sandboxing.

issues.title: from_prefixed_env does not filter to uppercase
issues.detail: Unlike every other loading method, `from_prefixed_env` stores keys exactly as found after stripping the prefix. If the env var is `FLASK_lower`, the key `lower` is stored, bypassing the uppercase-only convention.

children.title: Loading From Python Files
children.sub: Execute a Python config file as a module and extract its uppercase attributes.
children.detail: `from_pyfile` compiles and exec's the file as a module, then passes it to `from_object` which copies uppercase attributes into the Config dict.

code.label: from_pyfile — exec Python file, then from_object
from_file — open file, call load(), then from_mapping

rows.title: Resolve path
rows.detail: Join root_path with filename to get absolute path.

rows.title: Read and exec file
rows.detail: Open in binary, compile, exec into a fresh module’s __dict__.

rows.title: Filter to config
rows.detail: Pass the module to from_object, which copies uppercase attributes into the Config dict.

children.title: Loading From Objects
children.sub: Load uppercase attributes from a module, class, or import string.
children.detail: Accepts a Python object or dotted import string. Iterates `dir(obj)` and copies every attribute whose name passes `isupper()` into the Config dict.

code.label: from_object — import_string if str, then dir() + isupper filter

children.title: Structured File Loading
children.sub: Load JSON, TOML, or any format via a custom loader callable.
children.detail: Opens the file in text or binary mode, calls the user-provided `load` function, and passes the resulting mapping to `from_mapping` which filters to uppercase keys.

children.title: Environment Variables
children.sub: Load FLASK_* env vars with JSON parsing and nested dict support via double underscores.
children.detail: Iterates sorted env vars matching the prefix (default `FLASK_`), JSON-parses each value, and splits on `__` to create nested dicts.

issues.title: ErrorHandlerCallable takes Any instead of Exception
issues.detail: The error handler type uses `t.Any` for the exception argument because typing a specific exception class conflicts with decorating multiple times with different exception types. Three GitHub issues document this limitation.

children.sub: The re-exported names and the module-level CLI entry point.

AUTHORED.title: Defining Routes
AUTHORED.sub: Register URL rules, organise endpoints with blueprints, and use class-based views.
AUTHORED.detail: Routes are built on the `Scaffold` base class shared by `Flask` and `Blueprint`. Decorators like `@route` defer to `add_url_rule`, blueprints record deferred functions replayed at registration time, and `MethodView` maps HTTP verbs to instance methods.

group.note: Three independent capabilities: the base class, the blueprint layer, and class-based views.

The @route decorator — entry point for most routing

anatomy.caption: How the routing pieces inherit and connect at registration time
Registries initialised by Scaffold.__init__ and filled by decorators

children.title: Scaffold Base Class
children.sub: Shared routing decorators, registries, and path resolution used by both Flask and Blueprint.

group.note: Independent facets of the base class: the route decorator, the setup guard, hooks, and path resolution.

children.detail: `Scaffold` defines `@route`, `add_url_rule` (raises NotImplementedError), HTTP-verb shortcuts, error/hook decorators, and path properties; it initialises 7 registries (6 defaultdicts + 1 plain dict). App and Blueprint both inherit it.

class Flask(App) — inherits Scaffold via App

children.title: Route Registration
children.sub: The @route decorator, verb shortcuts, and the abstract add_url_rule method.
children.detail: `@route(rule)` pops `endpoint` from options and calls `self.add_url_rule(rule, endpoint, f)`. Scaffold's own `add_url_rule` raises `NotImplementedError`; the real implementation lives in `App.add_url_rule`.

code.label: @route decorator — parses rule and calls add_url_rule
App.add_url_rule — the real implementation that builds Rule objects

rows.detail: `@route('/path')` returns a decorator that pops `endpoint` from options.

rows.title: Calls add_url_rule

rows.title: App resolves methods
rows.detail: Defaults to GET; adds HEAD always, adds OPTIONS if `provide_automatic_options` is true.

rows.title: Rule added to url_map
rows.detail: `self.url_map.add(rule_obj)` and view stored in `self.view_functions[endpoint]`.

issues.title: Verb shortcuts reject extra methods argument
issues.detail: `_method_route` raises TypeError if `methods` is already in options, so `@app.get('/x', methods=['GET'])` fails even though it is redundant.

children.title: Setup Guard
children.sub: The @setupmethod decorator prevents route registration after the first request.
children.detail: Every routing and hook method is wrapped by `@setupmethod`, which calls `self._check_setup_finished`. On `App` this raises after the first request; on `Blueprint` it raises after the first `register()` call.

code.label: setupmethod decorator — wraps f to call _check_setup_finished

anatomy.caption: What the guard checks for each subclass

children.title: Hooks & Error Handlers
children.sub: before_request, after_request, teardown, and errorhandler decorators appending to scoped registries.
children.detail: Each decorator appends a callable to its scope-keyed defaultdict (scope `None` = app-wide). Error handlers go through `_get_exc_class_and_code` to normalise int codes into `HTTPException` subclasses.

anatomy.caption: Lifecycle hooks in execution order (at request time)

issues.title: Passing an exception instance is a confusing TypeError
issues.detail: `_get_exc_class_and_code` checks `isinstance(exc_class, Exception)` after resolving codes, but the error message says 'is an instance, not a class' — easy to hit by accident with `@errorhandler(ValueError())`.

children.title: Path Resolution
children.sub: Locating a package's filesystem root from its import name using importlib.
children.detail: `_find_package_path` uses `importlib.util.find_spec` to locate the module root, falling back to `os.getcwd()` when the spec cannot be found. `find_package` then determines if the package is system-installed, in a venv, or local.

code.label: find_package — distinguishes system, venv, and local installs

rows.title: find_spec on root module
rows.detail: Extracts the root module name from `import_name` and calls `importlib.util.find_spec`.

rows.title: Namespace vs package vs module
rows.detail: Handles namespace packages (origin is None), regular packages (__init__.py), and plain modules differently.

rows.title: Fallback to cwd
rows.detail: If spec is None or ImportError, returns `os.getcwd()`.

children.title: Blueprints
children.sub: Group routes under a name and URL prefix, then register them all at once on a Flask app.

group.note: Three facets: the deferred-recording mechanism, the registration procedure, and the IO layer.

children.detail: A `Blueprint` records decorator calls as deferred functions. When `app.register_blueprint(bp)` is called, a `BlueprintSetupState` replays each one, prefixing URL rules and endpoint names.

code.label: Blueprint.register — replay deferred functions, nest children
IO Blueprint — adds CLI group and send_static_file

anatomy.caption: How a blueprint route ends up in the app's url_map
Two-layer blueprint: sansio (protocol) and IO (static/CLI)

children.title: Deferred Recording
children.sub: Blueprint.add_url_rule records a lambda instead of registering immediately.
children.detail: Blueprint overrides `add_url_rule` to call `self.record(lambda s: s.add_url_rule(...))`, appending the lambda to `self.deferred_functions`. `record_once` wraps the function so it runs only on first registration.

code.label: record and record_once — append to deferred_functions

anatomy.caption: What gets deferred vs applied immediately

issues.title: Dot in endpoint or view name raises ValueError
issues.detail: Blueprint.add_url_rule checks for '.' in endpoint and view_func.__name__, raising ValueError. This prevents dotted endpoints, since dots collide with the blueprint.endpoint naming scheme.

children.title: Registration Procedure
children.sub: Blueprint.register replays deferred functions, merges hooks, and nests child blueprints.
children.detail: `register()` creates a `BlueprintSetupState`, merges error handlers and hooks into the app under the blueprint's name prefix, replays all deferred functions, and recursively registers nested blueprints.

code.label: _merge_blueprint_funcs — copies hooks into app under namespaced keys

rows.title: Check for duplicate name
rows.detail: Raises ValueError if the name (including prefix) is already in `app.blueprints`.

rows.title: Create setup state
rows.detail: `make_setup_state(app, options)` — stores url_prefix, subdomain, url_defaults.

rows.title: Add static route
rows.detail: If `has_static_folder`, registers `<prefix>/static/<path:filename>` → `send_static_file`.

rows.title: Merge hooks
rows.detail: `_merge_blueprint_funcs` copies before/after/teardown/error handlers into app under `name.` scope.

rows.title: Replay deferred functions
rows.detail: Each lambda in `deferred_functions` is called with the setup state.

rows.title: Register nested blueprints
rows.detail: Iterates `self._blueprints`, composes prefixes and subdomains, calls `blueprint.register()` recursively.

issues.title: Registering same blueprint name twice raises
issues.detail: Since 2.1, re-registering a blueprint under the same name raises ValueError. The same object can be registered under a different `name=` override, but the original name slot is permanently taken.

children.title: IO Layer
children.sub: The concrete Blueprint class adds static-file serving, resource file access, and a CLI command group.
children.detail: The IO `Blueprint` inherits the sansio `Blueprint` and adds `send_static_file`, `get_send_file_max_age`, `open_resource`, and a Click `AppGroup` for CLI commands.

code.label: send_static_file — serves from static_folder via send_from_directory
open_resource — opens files relative to root_path, read-only

rows.label: Cache control
rows.value: SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT config; None means conditional requests

rows.label: CLI group
rows.value: self.cli = AppGroup(); merged into app.cli during register()

children.title: Class-Based Views
children.sub: View and MethodView let you define route handlers as classes instead of plain functions.

group.note: Two view classes: generic View and HTTP-verb-dispatching MethodView.

children.detail: `View` provides `as_view()` to convert a class into a view function for `add_url_rule`. `MethodView` extends it to auto-dispatch to `get()`, `post()`, etc. based on `request.method`.

code.label: View class — base with dispatch_request and class attributes
View.as_view — factory that produces a route-callable closure

anatomy.caption: How View.as_view produces a route-callable function
Class attributes that control View behavior
rows: Applied in order to the generated view function
False reuses one instance across requests

children.title: View & as_view
children.sub: Generic base class with the as_view() factory that creates route-callable closures.
children.detail: `as_view(name)` creates a closure that instantiates the class (or reuses one if `init_every_request` is False) and calls `dispatch_request`. Decorators from `cls.decorators` are applied, and metadata like `view_class` is attached.

code.label: as_view — two branches: init_every_request True vs False
init_every_request=True branch: new instance per request
Apply decorators, attach view_class and methods

rows.title: Choose instantiation strategy
rows.detail: If `init_every_request` is True, the closure creates a new instance per call; otherwise one is created at as_view time.

rows.title: Apply decorators
rows.detail: Each decorator in `cls.decorators` wraps the view closure in list order.

rows.title: Attach metadata
rows.detail: `view.view_class`, `view.methods`, `view.provide_automatic_options` are set for Flask inspection.

children.title: MethodView Dispatch
children.sub: Automatically routes HTTP verbs to same-name instance methods.
children.detail: `__init_subclass__` scans for methods named after HTTP verbs and auto-populates the `methods` set. `dispatch_request` calls `getattr(self, request.method.lower())`, falling back from HEAD to GET.

code.label: dispatch_request — getattr by method name, HEAD→GET fallback
http_method_funcs — the frozenset of recognised verb names

anatomy.caption: Recognised HTTP method names (http_method_funcs)
How dispatch_request resolves the handler

issues.title: Missing handler triggers assert, not 405
issues.detail: If a MethodView subclass does not define a handler for the matched HTTP method, `dispatch_request` hits `assert meth is not None` — raising AssertionError (500) instead of returning a proper 405 Method Not Allowed.

AUTHORED.title: Handling Requests
AUTHORED.sub: Push contexts, access request and session globals, serve files, flash messages, and handle errors at runtime.
AUTHORED.detail: Every incoming WSGI request creates an `AppContext` holding the app, request, session and `g`. The context is pushed onto a `ContextVar`, making five proxies (`current_app`, `request`, `session`, `g`, `app_ctx`) available anywhere in the call stack.

group.note: Six capabilities a developer uses at runtime; only the context lifecycle is sequential.

anatomy.caption: How a WSGI request flows through context, dispatch, and response
One request from arrival to response

rows.label: push(): set _cv_app, open session, match URL
rows.note: Session loaded lazily on first access after push

children.title: Context Lifecycle
children.sub: The unified AppContext that makes app, request, session, and g available per-request.
children.detail: Since Flask 3.2, `AppContext` merges the old app and request contexts. One `ContextVar` (`_cv_app`) stores the active context; `push()` sets it, `pop()` resets it and runs teardown callbacks.

code.label: AppContext class docstring and version history
push(): set ContextVar, open session, match URL
pop(): teardown request, teardown app, reset ContextVar

rows.title: Create context
rows.detail: AppContext.from_environ builds a Request from the WSGI environ and stores it alongside app, g, and url_adapter.

rows.title: Push
rows.detail: _cv_app.set(self), send appcontext_pushed signal, open session (lazy), match URL via url_adapter.

rows.title: Handle request
rows.detail: All code runs inside this context; proxies resolve through _cv_app.

rows.title: Pop
rows.detail: do_teardown_request, request.close(), do_teardown_appcontext, _cv_app.reset(), appcontext_popped signal.

anatomy.caption: What the context holds

children.title: Push And Match
children.sub: Activating the context, opening the session, and performing URL routing.
children.detail: `push()` guards against redundant activation via `_cv_token`; on first push it sets the ContextVar, sends `appcontext_pushed`, lazy-loads the session, and calls `match_request`. `_push_count` is only used in `pop()` to defer teardown.

code.label: push: set cv, signal, open session, match
match_request: url_adapter.match stores url_rule and view_args

rows.title: Increment push count
rows.detail: If already pushed (_cv_token not None), return immediately.

rows.title: Set ContextVar
rows.detail: _cv_app.set(self) — all proxies now resolve to this context.

rows.title: Send signal
rows.detail: appcontext_pushed.send(self.app).

rows.title: Open session
rows.detail: Calls session_interface.open_session; falls back to NullSession if it returns None.

rows.title: Match URL
rows.detail: url_adapter.match() stores url_rule and view_args on request, or stores routing_exception.

children.title: Pop And Teardown
children.sub: Deactivating the context and running all cleanup callbacks.
children.detail: `pop()` decrements `_push_count`; cleanup runs only when count reaches zero. It runs request teardown, app teardown, resets the ContextVar, and sends `appcontext_popped`.

code.label: pop: guard count, teardown request, teardown app, reset cv
do_teardown_request: blueprint + app teardown funcs, signal

rows.title: Guard
rows.detail: Raises RuntimeError if not pushed or not the active context.

rows.title: Decrement count
rows.detail: If _push_count > 0 after decrement, return without cleanup.

rows.title: Teardown request
rows.detail: app.do_teardown_request runs blueprint and app teardown funcs, sends request_tearing_down.

rows.title: Close request
rows.detail: request.close() releases resources.

rows.title: Teardown app context
rows.detail: app.do_teardown_appcontext runs app teardown funcs, sends appcontext_tearing_down.

rows.title: Reset ContextVar
rows.detail: _cv_app.reset(token), send appcontext_popped signal.

children.title: Background Tasks
children.sub: Helpers that preserve request context for streaming and background work.
children.detail: `copy_current_request_context` snapshots the context for background threads; `stream_with_context` re-pushes it so streaming generators keep access to request and session.

code.label: copy_current_request_context: copies context for background tasks
stream_with_context: re-pushes context around a generator
AppContext.copy(): creates new context with same request/session

anatomy.caption: Two context-preservation helpers
rows: Calls ctx.copy(), pushes the copy with `with`
Re-pushes current context inside a wrapper generator

issues.title: Session modification in background tasks is unsafe
issues.detail: Both helpers warn that modifying the session in the child may happen after the Set-Cookie header is already written. The change is silently lost.

children.title: Global Proxies
children.sub: Thread-local-like proxies that resolve the active app, request, session, and g from a ContextVar.
children.detail: Five `LocalProxy` objects all read from one `ContextVar[AppContext]` named `_cv_app`, each dereferencing a different attribute. Accessing any proxy outside a pushed context raises a `RuntimeError`.

anatomy.caption: The five global proxies

rows.value: werkzeug.local.LocalProxy with typed subclass (FlaskProxy, RequestProxy, etc.)

rows.value: request_ctx is aliased to app_ctx with a DeprecationWarning; removed in Flask 4.0

issues.title: Deprecated request_ctx still importable
issues.detail: The module __getattr__ silently redirects `request_ctx` to `app_ctx` with a DeprecationWarning. Code relying on `request_ctx` identity will break in Flask 4.0.

children.title: Request & Response
children.sub: Flask's Request and Response wrappers that extend Werkzeug with app-config-aware properties.
children.detail: `Request` adds URL-routing attributes (`url_rule`, `view_args`, `routing_exception`) and config-backed size limits. `Response` defaults to `text/html` mimetype and reads `MAX_COOKIE_SIZE` from config.

code.label: Response: HTML default, max_cookie_size from config

anatomy.caption: Flask-specific Request attributes
rows: Blueprint chain from root to current

anatomy.caption: Config-backed size limits (per-request overridable since 3.1)

children.title: Session Management
children.sub: Signed-cookie sessions opened lazily on push and saved during response finalization.
children.detail: `SecureCookieSessionInterface` signs session data with `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer`, using a `CallbackDict` that auto-sets `modified=True` on writes. When `secret_key` is missing, a `NullSession` blocks writes with a `RuntimeError`.

code.label: NullSession: raises RuntimeError on any write
get_signing_serializer: builds URLSafeTimedSerializer with fallback keys
open_session: deserialise signed cookie, return empty on bad signature

anatomy.caption: Session open and save flow
Session cookie configuration (all from app.config)
rows: Re-set cookie every request if permanent

issues.title: Bad signatures silently create empty sessions
issues.detail: When open_session catches a BadSignature (tampered or expired cookie), it returns a brand-new empty session with no warning. The user loses all session data without explanation.

issues.title: NullSession allows reads of empty dict
issues.detail: When secret_key is unset, a NullSession is created that allows read access (returning empty values) but raises RuntimeError only on writes. Code that checks for session keys silently gets False/None rather than an error.

children.title: Request Helpers
children.sub: Convenience functions for URL generation, redirects, aborting, message flashing, and file serving.
children.detail: Thin wrappers that delegate to `current_app` methods or Werkzeug utilities. Each reads from the context to inject Flask-specific configuration automatically.

code.label: make_response: converts view return into Response

anatomy.caption: Helper functions available inside a request context
How flash() and get_flashed_messages() use session and app_ctx

issues.title: send_file trusts caller-provided paths
issues.detail: The docstring warns 'never pass file paths provided by a user' but there is no runtime guard in send_file itself. Only send_from_directory uses safe_join. A caller passing user input directly to send_file creates a path traversal vulnerability.

children.title: Debug Helpers
children.sub: Improved error messages and template loading diagnostics active only in debug mode.
children.detail: In debug mode, Flask patches `request.files` to explain missing enctype, intercepts routing redirects that would drop POST data, and logs template-loader diagnostics. The logging module provides a request-aware error stream.

code.label: FormDataRoutingRedirect: warns about POST data loss

anatomy.caption: Debug-mode enhancements
rows: Raises error explaining data will be dropped
Template loading fails or is ambiguous
Logs every loader tried with detail
Any log output during a request

rows.label: Debug log level

AUTHORED.title: Rendering Responses
AUTHORED.sub: Render Jinja2 templates and serialise JSON, including the tagged-JSON codec used by sessions.
AUTHORED.detail: Four modules turn application data into response bodies: a Jinja2 environment with dispatching loader, a pluggable JSON provider, public convenience functions, and a tagged serialiser for sessions.

code.label: render_template — main public API for templates
jsonify — main public API for JSON responses
JSONProvider base class, stored on app.json

group.note: Templates, JSON API, provider, and tagged serialiser are independent subsystems, not a pipeline.

anatomy.caption: How templates and JSON flow from app code to responses

children.title: Template Rendering
children.sub: Jinja2 environment setup, template loading from app and blueprints, and rendering pipeline.
children.detail: Templates are loaded through a `DispatchingJinjaLoader` whose `_iter_loaders` yields the app's loader first, then each blueprint's. Context processors inject `g`, `request`, and custom variables before rendering.

code.label: _iter_loaders: yields app loader first, then blueprints

group.note: Independent aspects of the templating subsystem: environment setup, loading, rendering pipeline, and public API.

anatomy.caption: How a template name reaches rendered HTML
Globals injected into every Jinja environment

children.sub: Dispatching loader searches app folder first, then every registered blueprint.

issues.detail: In fast mode the app loader is tried first, so an app template always wins over a blueprint template with the same name. In explained mode a warning is logged for multiple matches, but in fast mode the shadow is silent.

children.title: Render Pipeline
children.sub: Context injection, before and after signals, and the final template render call.
children.detail: Both render and stream follow the same pattern: get the app context, update template context with processors, send `before_render_template`, render or generate, then send `template_rendered`.

code.label: _stream: same but yields chunks, signal after last chunk
update_template_context: runs all processors, user values win

rows.title: Get app context
rows.detail: Reads app_ctx._get_current_object() to get the concrete AppContext.

rows.title: Resolve template
rows.detail: Calls jinja_env.get_or_select_template (by name) or from_string (for source strings).

rows.title: Update context
rows.detail: Runs context processors (None key + blueprint chain). User-passed values override processor values.

rows.title: Send before_render_template
rows.detail: Blinker signal with app, template, and context.

rows.title: Render or stream
rows.detail: template.render(context) returns a string; template.generate(context) yields chunks wrapped in stream_with_context.

rows.title: Send template_rendered
rows.detail: Sent after render returns or after the last streamed chunk.

children.title: JSON Public Functions
children.sub: Module-level convenience functions that delegate to the current app's JSON provider or fall back to stdlib.
children.detail: Five functions: `dumps`, `dump`, `loads`, `load`, and `jsonify`. The first four check `current_app` and delegate to `app.json.*`, falling back to stdlib; `jsonify` always requires an app context.

issues.title: jsonify crashes without app context
issues.detail: Unlike dumps and loads which fall back to stdlib, jsonify unconditionally accesses current_app.json.response. Calling it outside a request or app context raises a RuntimeError with no fallback.

children.title: Tagged JSON Serialiser
children.sub: Lossless codec for non-JSON types used by Flask's session cookie interface.
children.detail: `TaggedJSONSerializer` wraps values in single-key dicts (tags like `" t"`, `" b"`, `" d"`) so tuples, bytes, UUIDs, datetimes, and Markup survive a JSON round-trip. Used by `SecureCookieSessionInterface`.

code.label: register: add a new tag, with force and index

notes.label: outer key " t"

notes.value: datetime tag, value is an HTTP-date string

notes.label: plain string
notes.value: no tag needed, passes through as-is

rows.title: Tag the value
rows.detail: Walk the object recursively; each non-JSON type is wrapped in a single-key dict whose key is the tag.

rows.title: Dump to JSON
rows.detail: Calls flask.json.dumps with compact separators — the tagged structure is now pure JSON.

rows.title: Load from JSON
rows.detail: Calls flask.json.loads to parse the JSON string back to dicts and lists.

rows.title: Untag scan
rows.detail: Walks every dict and list recursively; single-key dicts whose key is a registered tag are converted back to the original Python type.

issues.title: Tag order determines which type wins
issues.detail: TagDict must come before PassDict, and TagTuple before PassList, because the first matching tag wins. A custom tag registered at the wrong index can silently be shadowed by PassDict or PassList, losing type fidelity.

issues.title: PYTHONSTARTUP is eval'd with exec mode
issues.detail: The startup file is compiled with `exec` mode and run via `eval`, executing arbitrary code in the shell context dict. This is standard Python behavior but means a malicious PYTHONSTARTUP runs with full access when `flask shell` is invoked.

AUTHORED.sub: Three bundled examples — the Flaskr tutorial blog, a Celery task-queue integration, and a JavaScript fetch demo.

group.note: Three independent demo apps; no ordering or dependency between them.

children.title: Flaskr Tutorial Blog
children.sub: A multi-user blog with registration, login, and CRUD posts backed by SQLite.

group.note: Blueprints and database layer initialised together by the factory; no runtime ordering between them.

children.detail: The `create_app` factory sets a default `SECRET_KEY` of `"dev"`, registers the db teardown, and mounts the `auth` and `blog` blueprints. The root `/` is aliased to `blog.index`.

issues.title: Hardcoded default SECRET_KEY
issues.detail: SECRET_KEY defaults to the string "dev". If the instance config.py is never created (silent=True ignores its absence), sessions are signed with a publicly known key.

children.title: Authentication
children.sub: Registration, login, logout and the login_required decorator.
children.detail: The `auth` blueprint at `/auth` handles user creation with hashed passwords, session-based login, and a `before_app_request` hook that loads the current user into `g.user` on every request.

issues.detail: load_logged_in_user runs a SELECT on the user table for every request across the entire app, including unauthenticated and static routes, because it is registered as a before_app_request hook.

children.sub: Per-request SQLite connection management, schema init, and a CLI command.
children.detail: `get_db` stores a SQLite connection on Flask's `g` object so every call within one request reuses it. `close_db` is registered as a teardown, and the `init-db` CLI command runs `schema.sql`.
